description: Submit proof: a first-party URL (brand or restaurant page, PDF, CSV), or label photos (base64; several sides of one package beat one photo), with your reading of it. A URL is a citation: we never download it. Values that fill gaps publish at once, marked unverified; they become verified when an agent with a different owner finds its own proof of the item and reads the same values exactly, with the later verifying reader email-verified at submission and old enough under its plan. No-email readings never verify another reader. Contribution work costs no read units. A label photo is re-encoded and read by OCR on our server (no model): a field the label text states the same value for is marked photo_confirmed, which is more than unverified and less than verified. Values that would replace existing contributed ones wait for that verification. Values imported from a source (verification "source") are authoritative and never replaced: a contradicting reading is kept beside them; flag a source value you believe wrong. An item the database lacks (a restaurant dish, a new or small-brand product, a supplement) is created with new_entity in place of id, with market and your reading; it publishes at once as unverified and is verified the same way. First-party sources are the strongest proof. Share-alike sources (Open Food Facts, Wikipedia) are refused. Text addressed to AI agents in a proof quarantines it.

id.description: The entity this proves. Give id, or new_entity to create one; a proof with neither waits for a reader to name one.

linked_from.description: When the url is a file on another host (a shared CDN such as cdn.sanity.io, a document host): the page on the brand's or restaurant's own site that links to it, which you followed to reach the file. Trust follows that page: a file linked from an approved first-party domain is first-party (rank 1); the file's host alone never is. Omit when the url is on the owner's own domain.

market.description: ISO 3166-1 country the label is for, e.g. US, GB, JP. Required with new_entity: it becomes the item's market.

new_entity.description: The item to create when it does not exist yet: search and lookup_barcode first. It publishes at once as unverified, with its values, and a blind second reader verifies it like them. An obvious duplicate (same barcode in the same market, or same brand and name) is refused with the id to use.

barcode.description: GTIN (UPC-A, EAN-13, GTIN-14) as printed. Normalised and check-digit tested.

basis.description: Products only: per_100ml for a liquid sold by volume. Supplements and menu items are per serving.

brand.description: The brand, or the restaurant for a menu item. Linked to the existing brand or chain with that name, or created.

kind.description: product: a packaged food with a nutrition panel (stored per 100 g); supplement: a Supplement Facts panel (per serving); menu_item: a restaurant or chain item (per serving).

lang.description: Language of the name, BCP 47. Defaults to en.

name.description: The item's name as printed, without the brand: "Chocolate Chip" for a Clif Bar, "Big Mac" for McDonald's.

grams.description: Its weight in grams, when printed.

label.description: The serving as printed, e.g. "1 bar (68 g)".

ml.description: Its volume in millilitres, when printed. Converts per-serving values on a per_100ml item.

page.description: For a PDF: the page the values are printed on, as the PDF viewer numbers it. Kept with the url as #page=N.

read_at.description: The date you read the page, YYYY-MM-DD. Today when absent.

reading.description: Your reading of the proof. Needs id or new_entity.

outcome.description: Truthful abstention: omit values and serving measurements. Recorded, never agreement or credit.

serving_grams.description: Grams in one serving, exactly as printed on the proof; leave it out when the label prints no grams. Needed to store per-serving values per 100 g. Readers must match it exactly, like any other value.

serving_ml.description: Millilitres in one serving, exactly as printed on the proof ("1 can (473 mL)"); leave it out when the label prints no volume. Needed to store per-serving values per 100 ml (a drink sold by volume). Readers must match it exactly, like serving_grams.

values.description: Exactly what the proof states, one entry per value, on the basis printed (per_serving for a per-serving column).

bound.description: When the label states a bound, not a value: "<1 g" is bound "lt" with value 1; "trace" uses value 0. A printed interval uses two entries of the same property and basis, lower ge/gt and upper le/lt; get retains both in bounds.

property.description: A registry key (see describe), or any other line the label prints, by its name as printed ("Creatine Monohydrate"): a free label line. A free line needs a number and a unit (g, mg, mcg, IU, CFU, billion CFU or ml); it is stored under line:<name> (lower case, spaces collapsed, ® and ™ removed), served at once with its identity unverified, and adds up with every line of the same name.

regime.description: Labelling regime of the label if known (US, EU, UK, ...). Detected when absent.

source_date.description: The effective or publication date stated by the source, YYYY-MM-DD. Omit when unknown; never use the date you read it.

source_version.description: The edition or version printed by the source. Omit when unknown.

url.description: A link to the proof: the brand's or restaurant's own page, its PDF or a regulator's record. It is kept as a citation, as text with the date you read it; our server never visits it. A first-party PDF is cited by url and page, never uploaded. An agent verifying the item receives this citation only with explicit open_links: true.

name: add_proof
